style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">Total gross unrecognized tax benefits of $0.6&#160;million are reflected in the Company&#8217;s December&#160;31, 2020 consolidated balance sheet as deferred income taxes.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">The amount of unrecognized tax benefits, including accrued interest, penalties and federal tax benefit, which, if ultimately recognized, could affect the effective tax rate in a future period are $0.5&#160;million, $0.7&#160;million and $1.8&#160;million as of December&#160;31, 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">The Company does not expect any material changes to its tax uncertainties within the 12-month rolling period ending December&#160;31, 2021.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">Interest expense and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits are recognized as part of the provision for income taxes. Gross interest and penalties of $0.0&#160;million, $0.1&#160;million and $0.9&#160;million are provided for within the liability for unrecognized tax benefits as of December&#160;31, 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, federal net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $188.9&#160;million are available to offset future federal taxable income. Net operating loss carryforwards of $92.7&#160;million will expire during the Company&#8217;s 2037 tax&#160;year. Due to the enactment of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, federal net operating losses generated beginning in 2018 and thereafter are carried forward indefinitely. Therefore, the remaining $96.2&#160;million of net operating loss carryforwards will not expire.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">The Company files federal and state income tax returns in jurisdictions with varying statutes of limitations expiration dates. The Company&#8217;s calendar 2016 through 2020 tax&#160;years generally remain subject to examination by tax authorities. The Internal Revenue Service closed their examination of the calendar 2017 tax year during the year ended December 31, 2020. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">Net income tax payments were $3.2&#160;million, $0.1&#160;million and $0.1&#160;million for the&#160;years ended December&#160;31, 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"><font style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-left:0pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</font></p><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:0pt;">8.</p></td><td style="padding:0pt;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:0pt;">LEASES</p></td></tr></table><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">The Company leases all its facilities. The Company&#8217;s real estate lease portfolio primarily consists of modified gross leases, in which the Company pays a share of the operating costs, and triple-net leases, in which the Company pays all of the operating costs. Operating costs that are the responsibility of the Company include taxes, maintenance, insurance and other allowable expenses. These expenses are considered variable costs as they are not tied to an index or rate. In addition, delivery vehicles and office equipment are leased under operating leases. Lease terms are generally five&#160;years or less with renewal options for additional periods and often contain early termination clauses. Rents are generally increased annually by amounts stated within individual agreements, subject to certain maximum amounts defined within individual agreements.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">The Company also leases certain patient equipment. Lease terms are generally twelve&#160;months or less with renewal options for additional periods. The Company also has short-term patient equipment leases with certain suppliers that are entirely variable based on equipment usage or a&#160;percentage of net revenues collected for specific products. Patient equipment lease expense is recorded in product and supply costs in the consolidated statements of income in the period incurred. The Company uses the portfolio approach to review patient equipment leases.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">All of the Company&#8217;s leases are classified as operating leases. The leases do not include options to purchase the underlying assets that the Company is reasonably certain to exercise. The components of lease assets and liabilities are included on the consolidated balance sheets.</p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt;"><font style="margin-bottom:12pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</font></p><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:0pt;">9.</p></td><td style="padding:0pt;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Litigation</b>&#8212; On December&#160;18, 2020, a federal judge approved a civil and administrative settlement Apria recently entered into with the United States and state Medicaid programs in a complaint filed by three relators under the qui tam provisions of the False Claims Act (&#8220;FCA&#8221;), 31 U.S.C. &#167; 3729 et seq., as well as comparable state false claims laws, in connection with the rental of non-invasive ventilators (&#8220;NIVs&#8221;). Apria also entered into separate settlements to resolve the relators&#8217; claims brought on behalf of the States of California and Illinois related to NIV covered by private insurers. The matter had been pending since 2017. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">The government had alleged that Apria violated the FCA by submitting false claims seeking reimbursement for NIVs which were not being used, or not being used sufficiently, by patients, for NIVs which were being used pursuant to physician orders on a device setting which was available from other less expensive devices, and for improperly waiving co-pays to induce beneficiaries to rent NIVs. To resolve any potential liability, Apria agreed to </p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">F-28</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">enter into a civil settlement agreement with the government and paid $40.0 million to the federal government and the states during the year ended December 31, 2020. Apria separately agreed with the relators and paid approximately $3.6 million during the year ended December 31, 2020 to settle all remaining claims from their complaint, including: (1)&#160;claims for retaliation in violation of federal and state laws; (2)&#160;claims for attorneys&#8217; fees and costs available under federal and state law; and (3)&#160;claims under the Illinois Insurance Claims Fraud Prevention Act, 740 ILL. COMP. STAT. 92/1 et seq. Apria also agreed with the California Department of Insurance to pay $0.5 million, which is recorded as a current liability on the consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2020, to resolve claims asserted by the relators under the California Insurance Frauds Prevention Act, CAL. INS. CODE &#167; 1871 et seq. Apria did not admit that any of its conduct was illegal or otherwise improper. The expense is included in selling, distribution and administrative expenses in the consolidated statements of income and was $31.9&#160;million, $12.2&#160;million, and $0.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively.&#160; </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">In addition to the matter referenced in this note, the Company is engaged in the defense of certain claims and lawsuits arising out of the ordinary course and conduct of its business, the outcomes of which are not determinable at this time. Insurance policies covering such potential losses, where such coverage is cost effective, are maintained. In the opinion of management, any liability that might be incurred upon the resolution of these claims and lawsuits will not, in the aggregate, have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s financial condition or results of operations, cash flows and liquidity. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Supplier Concentration</b>&#8212;Currently, approximately 76% of purchases for patient equipment and supplies are from five vendors. Although there are a limited number of suppliers, management believes that other vendors could provide similar products on comparable terms. However, a change in suppliers could cause delays in service delivery and possible losses of revenue, which could adversely affect the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial condition or operating results. In addition, from time to time, the Company enters into exclusive arrangements with certain suppliers to provide patient equipment and supplies.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Purchase Obligations</b>&#8212;In April&#160;2009, the Company entered into a ten-year information technology services agreement to outsource certain information systems functions. The Company did not receive any proceeds from the shares sold by the selling stockholders and the Company incurred offering related expenses of approximately $6.0 million, of which $3.3 million was expense in selling, distribution, and administrative expenses on the consolidated statement of income during the year end December 31, 2020.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;"><font style="white-space:pre-wrap;">In connection with the completion of the offering, the Company underwent a reorganization transaction. On February 10, 2021, a newly formed indirect subsidiary of Apria, Inc. merged with and into the Company, with the Company surviving. As a result, the Company became an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Apria, Inc.  Our shareholders who previously held their ownership interest prior to the IPO through Apria Holdings LLC (as the 100% direct owner of the Company) received an aggregate of 35,210,915 shares of newly issued common stock of Apria, Inc. with a par value of $0.01 per share.  The merger was accounted for as a reorganization of entities under common control. As a result, the consolidated financial statements of Apria, Inc. will recognize the assets and liabilities received in the merger at their historical carrying amounts as reflected in the historical consolidated financial statements of the Company, the accounting predecessor.</font></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;"><font style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The secondary offering triggered a pre-existing provision in the SARs under which the SARs became exercisable by holders upon IPO.  As a result of the SARs becoming exercisable upon the IPO, the total 3,766,228 SARs issued will become potentially dilutive instruments for purposes of Apria, Inc.&#8217;s earnings per share.  In addition, the secondary offering triggered a pre-existing provision under the Company&#8217;s 2019 LTIP pursuant to which the incentive awards will be settled in shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock.  The number of shares to be received will be determined by dividing the amount of each executive&#8217;s earned award by the volume-weighted average price of a share of common stock over the first 20 trading days following the offering. Awards granted under the 2019 LTIP have a maximum value of $4.4 million. The offering was accounted for as a modification and the 2019 LTIP awards will be reclassified from a liability to equity classified award.</font></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"><font style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The secondary offering also resulted in the grant of restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) to the Company&#8217;s Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;). The RSUs vest in tranches, with the first tranche vesting immediately upon the completion of the offering and the remaining RSUs vesting in two equal tranches upon the six month and first year anniversary following the offering, subject to the CFO&#8217;s continued employment. Each tranche of RSUs can be settled in either cash or shares of our common stock at the election of the CFO. The total value of RSUs granted to the CFO was $3.2 million, of which $1.6 million was paid in cash at the IPO related to the first tranche of vested RSUs. The $1.6 million cash paid to the CFO will be recognized as compensation expense in Selling, distribution and administrative expenses.  The remaining RSUs will be liability classified because they are settleable in cash or shares at the CFO&#8217;s election, which is outside of the control of the Company, and will be included in the current portion of other accrued liabilities. </font></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><font style="background-color:#ffff00;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</font></p><p style="display:none;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';line-height:0pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt;"><font style="font-size:0pt;margin-bottom:12pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</font></p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">F-31</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Item&#160;<a name="Item9ChangesinandDisagreementswithAccoun"></a>9. Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">None</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Item&#160;<a name="Item9AControlsandProcedures_983072"></a>9A. Controls and Procedures</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Disclosure Controls and Procedures</b><font style="font-size:12pt;"> </font></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The Company maintains a set of disclosure controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by the Company in reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act, is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in SEC rules and forms. Any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance of achieving the desired control objectives. The Company&#8217;s management, with the participation of the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer, and the Company&#8217;s Chief Financial Officer, has evaluated the effectiveness of the design and operation of the Company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Based upon that evaluation, the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer and the Company&#8217;s Chief Financial Officer concluded that, as of December 31, 2020, the Company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective to accomplish their objectives at the reasonable assurance level.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Management&#8217;s Annual Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements in accordance with GAAP. We are currently in the process of reviewing, documenting and testing our internal control over financial reporting.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We have not performed an evaluation of our internal control over financial reporting, such as required by Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, nor have we engaged an independent registered public accounting firm to perform an audit of our internal control over financial reporting as of any balance sheet date or for any period reported in our financial statements. This annual report does not include a report of management&#8217;s assessment regarding internal control over financial reporting or an attestation report of the company&#8217;s registered public accounting firm due to a transition period established by rules of the SEC for newly public companies.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">There has been no change in our internal control over financial reporting during our most recent fiscal quarter that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Item&#160;<a name="Item9BOtherInformation_699247"></a>9B. style="margin-top:12pt;"></div><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Controlled Company Exception</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">As of the date of this report, our Sponsor holds more than a majority of the voting power of our common stock eligible to vote in the election of our directors. As a result, we are a &#8220;controlled company&#8221; within the meaning of the Nasdaq corporate governance standards. Under these corporate governance standards, a company of which more than 50% of the voting power is held by an individual, group or another company is a &#8220;controlled company&#8221; and may elect not to comply with certain corporate governance standards, including the requirements (1)&#160;that a majority of our board of directors consist of independent directors, (2)&#160;that our board of directors have a compensation committee that is comprised entirely of independent directors with a written charter addressing the committee&#8217;s purpose and responsibilities and (3)&#160;that our director nominations be made, or recommended to our full board of directors, by our independent directors or by a nominations committee that is comprised entirely of independent directors and that we adopt a written charter or board resolution addressing the nominations process. For at least some period following our IPO, we intend to utilize certain of these exemptions. Accordingly, you will not have the same protections afforded to </p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">86</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">stockholders of companies that are subject to all of these corporate governance requirements. As such, none of our directors, other than Messrs.&#160;Figueroa, Payson, Murphy and Zafirovski and Ms.&#160;Shapiro Snyder, received compensation for the&#160;year ended December&#160;31, 2020. Messrs.&#160;Payson, Murphy and Zafirovski and Ms.&#160;Shapiro Snyder were entitled to an annual cash retainer of $100,000, payable quarterly, for their service as a director during 2020. Mr.&#160;Figueroa was entitled to an annual cash retainer of $200,000 for his service as chairman of our Board of Directors during 2020. All of our directors are reimbursed for their reasonable out-of-pocket expenses related to their service as directors. In addition, Mr.&#160;Murphy and Ms.&#160;Shapiro Snyder were each granted SARs in 2019 and 2020. For a description of the vesting and other terms of the SARs granted to our directors, see &#8220;Narrative Disclosure to Summary Compensation Table and Grants of Plan-Based Awards in 2020 Table&#8212;Terms of Equity Awards&#8212;Stock Appreciation Rights of Apria Healthcare Group&#8221; below. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">On December&#160;4, 2020, our Board of Directors declared, and on December&#160;11, 2020 paid, a $201.79 per share dividend to common stockholders (the &#8220;2020 Dividend&#8221;). Under the terms of the 2015 Plan, an adjustment to the outstanding SARs was determined to be equitable and necessary in order to prevent the dilution or enlargement of benefits under the 2015 Plan. Holders of vested SARs were entitled to an immediate cash payment per SAR equal to the lower of (i)&#160;the per share dividend amount and (ii)&#160;an amount equal to the difference between $495.13 and the strike price of such vested SAR. Accordingly, Mr.&#160;Murphy and Ms.&#160;Shapiro Snyder each received a cash payment of $16,949 with respect to their vested SARs and the strike price for each vested SAR was reduced by an amount equal to the per share dividend amount less the cash payment per vested SAR. No cash payment was made with respect to their unvested SARs, but the strike price for each of their unvested SARs was reduced by the per share dividend amount. In accordance with FASB ASC Topic 718, changes to the SARs associated with the 2020 Dividend were accounted for as modifications. As such, the fair value of each award immediately before and after the modifications were compared and no incremental stock compensation was recognized.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We anticipate that we will review our director compensation program in connection with our IPO and make such changes as we determine are necessary or appropriate for our status as a public company.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Equity Units of BP Healthcare and Holdings</i>. In addition, we granted Dr.&#160;Payson an additional 3,830,365 Class&#160;B Units of BP Healthcare in connection with entering into a services agreement with him in November&#160;2012, in order to retain his services following his retirement as our Chief Executive Officer. Following our IPO, Dr.&#160;Payson&#8217;s BP Healthcare Units remained outstanding. In connection with Mr.&#160;Figueroa&#8217;s appointment as our Chief Executive Officer in 2012, he purchased 1,000,000 Class&#160;A-2 Units of Apria Holdings LLC (&#8220;Holdings&#8221;) and was also granted 12,257,169 Class&#160;B Units of Holdings. In connection with joining our Board of Directors in 2011, Mr.&#160;Zafirovski purchased 1,000,000 Class&#160;A-2 Units of Holdings and was also granted 5,030,651 Class&#160;B Units of Holdings. All of their respective Class&#160;A-2 Units were fully vested when purchased and all of their respective Class&#160;B Units are now fully vested (other than Mr.&#160;Zafirovski&#8217;s 3,353,767 target-based vesting Class&#160;B Units, which expired unvested).</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Termination, Clawback and Restrictive Covenants</i>. With respect to the Class&#160;B Units granted to Dr.&#160;Payson in 2012, if his services as a director are terminated by the Company for &#8220;cause&#8221; (as defined in his applicable subscription agreement) or by Dr.&#160;Payson when grounds exist for a termination for cause, then all of such vested Class&#160;B Units will be forfeited. If Mr.&#160;Zafirovski&#8217;s service as director is (1)&#160;terminated by us for &#8220;cause&#8221; (as defined in the applicable subscription agreement) or he voluntarily resigns where grounds for cause exist or (2)&#160;he breaches any of the restrictive covenants set forth below, then we have the right to purchase all of his vested Class&#160;B Units at the lesser of fair market value thereof and cost, which means that such vested Class&#160;B Units will be effectively forfeited.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">In certain circumstances the Company has the right to &#8220;clawback&#8221; and recover any gains Mr.&#160;Figueroa may have realized with respect to his Class&#160;B Units if he is terminated for &#8220;cause&#8221; (as such term was defined in his employment agreement) or he voluntarily resigns where grounds for cause exist and the Company notifies him of such fact within 30&#160;days of his resignation. Similarly, the Company has the right to &#8220;clawback&#8221; and recover any gains Mr.&#160;Zafirovski may have realized with respect to his Class&#160;B Units if he violates any of the restrictive covenants described below or we </p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">90</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">discover after a termination of employment that grounds existed for &#8220;cause&#8221; (as defined in his applicable subscription agreement).</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">As a condition of receiving their Class&#160;B Units, each of Dr.&#160;Payson, Mr.&#160;Figueroa and Mr.&#160;Zafirovski agreed to certain restrictive covenants, including confidentiality of information, non-disparagement (in the case of Messrs.&#160;Figueroa and Zafirovski), non-solicitation and non-competition covenants. The confidentiality covenant has an indefinite term, the non-disparagement covenant has an indefinite term (24&#160;months in the case of Mr.&#160;Figueroa), and the non-solicitation and non-competition covenants each have a term effective both during the term of the director&#8217;s term of service and for 12 (24&#160;months in the case of Mr.&#160;Figueroa) and 24&#160;months, respectively, following a termination of his services.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Conversion of Holdings Units. </i>In connection with our IPO, all Holdings Units held by our directors were surrendered in exchange for vested shares of our common stock. The number of vested shares of common stock delivered was determined in a manner intended to replicate the economic value associated with their Holdings Units, based upon the valuation derived from the IPO price.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The following table sets forth the number and value of vested shares of our style="margin-top:12pt;"></div><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We provide competitive base salaries and other benefits, including severance benefits, to attract and retain senior management talent. We have also used annual cash incentive compensation and long-term cash and equity incentives to ensure a performance-based delivery of pay that aligns as closely as possible the rewards of our named executive officers with the long-term interests of our equity-owners while enhancing executive retention.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We anticipate that we will continue to review our executive compensation programs in connection with our IPO and make such changes as are determined to be necessary or appropriate for our status as a public company. As we gain experience as a public company, we expect that the specific direction, emphasis and components of our executive compensation program will continue to evolve.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Compensation Determination Process.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Role of Board and Management. </i>Prior to our IPO, executive compensation and related decisions have been made by the Board of Directors of our subsidiary, Apria Healthcare Group. In connection with our IPO, our Board of Directors established a compensation committee that assumed responsibility for establishing, maintaining and administering our compensation and benefit policies. Except where the context requires otherwise, the terms &#8220;Board&#8221; or &#8220;Board of Directors&#8221; as used in this &#8220;Executive Compensation&#8221; section refer to the Board of Directors of Apria Healthcare Group.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Over the course of the&#160;year, Mr.&#160;Starck participates in discussions and deliberations with our Board of Directors regarding the determinations of annual cash incentive awards for our executives other than for himself. Specifically, he makes recommendations to our Board of Directors regarding the performance targets to be used under our annual executive bonus plan and the amounts of annual cash incentive awards and any discretionary bonus amounts to be made to our senior executives. Mr.&#160;Starck also makes recommendations to our Board of Directors regarding base salary adjustments for other executives based on their annual review of each executive&#8217;s performance. Our Board of Directors considers these recommendations and may exercise discretion in modifying them.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Employment Agreements. </font>For retention purposes, we entered into an employment agreement with Mr.&#160;Starck. A&#160;full description of the material terms of Mr.&#160;Starck&#8217;s employment agreement is presented below in the narrative section following the &#8220;Grants of Plan-Based Awards in 2020&#8221; table.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">Compensation Elements.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The following is a discussion and analysis of each component of our executive compensation program.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Base Salary</font><b style="font-weight:bold;">. </b>Base salary compensates executives for performing requirements of their positions and provides executives with a level of cash income predictability and stability with respect to a portion of their total compensation. Base salaries may be adjusted annually and, in certain circumstances, adjusted mid-year to deal with competitive </p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">92</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">pressures or changes in job responsibilities. In 2020, there were no changes to the base salaries of our named executive officers.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">Bonuses.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">2020 Annual Cash Incentive Compensation.</i> Annual cash incentive awards are available to our named executive officers under our annual executive bonus plan in order to motivate our executive officers to achieve short-term performance goals and tie a portion of their cash compensation to performance.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Executive Bonus Plan</i>. Under our Executive Bonus Plan for 2020 (the &#8220;2020 Bonus Plan&#8221;), each named executive officer who participated in the 2020 Bonus Plan was eligible to earn a cash incentive award based on achievement of performance targets for 2020.&#160;These performance targets were determined by our Board of Directors early in the&#160;year, after taking into consideration Mr.&#160;Starck&#8217;s recommendations and our budget for the&#160;year. The potential amount of the cash incentive award was based on a&#160;percentage of the executive officer&#8217;s base salary during 2020. The following table illustrates the 2020 potential target and maximum cash incentive awards expressed as a&#160;percentage of their base salaries for our named executive officers who were eligible to style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</font></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">In 2020, the cash incentive award opportunities were based on an EBIT target which accounted for 60% of the total award opportunity and a free cash flow target, which accounted for 40% of the total award opportunity. The Board of Directors has reserved the ability to adjust the actual fiscal&#160;year results to exclude the effects of extraordinary, unusual or infrequently occurring events. For purposes of the 2020 Bonus Plan, EBIT is calculated as net income for the period before the impact of interest income, interest expense and income taxes. The EBIT target excludes expenses incurred in relation to a series of civil investigative demands from the United States Attorney&#8217;s Office for the Southern District of New York (See &#8220;Item 3&#8212;Legal Proceedings&#8212;Civil Investigative Demand Issued by the United States Attorney&#8217;s Office for the Southern District of New York&#8221;) and expenses associated with the preparation to be a public company. Free cash flow is calculated as net cash provided by operating activities excluding term loan interest payments less net cash used in investing activities. The free cash flow target excludes payments for expenses related to a series of civil investigative demands from the United States Attorney&#8217;s Office for the Southern District of New York and payments for expenses associated with the preparation to be a public company.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Under our 2020 Bonus Plan, no cash incentive award was to be made with respect to any performance metric unless our actual EBITDA less Capex was at least $63.7&#160;million. For the 2020 Bonus Plan, EBITDA less Capex is calculated as EBITDA (as defined in the section entitled &#8220;Non-GAAP financial information&#8221;) less capital expenditures net of dispositions. For purposes of this metric &#8220;Capex&#8221; is defined as the value of the capital equipment received less the net book value of dispositions of capital equipment during the accounting period. The EBITDA less Capex target excludes expenses incurred in relation to a series of civil investigative demands from the United States Attorney&#8217;s Office for the Southern District of New York and expenses associated with the preparation to be a public company.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:24.5pt;margin:12pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">Payout percentages increased on a linear basis from 50% to 100% for EBIT metric achievement between $53.4 million and $62.8&#160;million and for free cash flow metric achievement between $50.2&#160;million and $59.0 million. If the Company achieved EBITDA less Capex of $70&#160;million, then payout percentages increased on a linear basis from 100% to the named executive officer&#8217;s applicable maximum bonus opportunity percentage for EBIT metric achievement between $63.4&#160;million and $75.4&#160;million and for free cash flow metric achievement between $59.6&#160;million and </p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">93</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">$70.8&#160;million. For 2020, the Company achieved EBITDA less Capex of $120.4 million. Accordingly, the named executive officers were eligible to receive cash incentive awards up to their applicable maximum bonus opportunity.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:24.5pt;margin:12pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">Actual results, payout percentages and the resulting achievement factors for the 2020 Bonus Plan were certified by the Board of Directors, as follows, based on the performance goals and funding scales described above. style="vertical-align:bottom;white-space:nowrap;width:10.9%;margin:0pt;padding:0pt;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><font style="font-size:11pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</font></p></td></tr></table></div><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><font style="font-size:1pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</font></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><font style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</font></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Other Cash Bonuses.</i> From time to time, we may award sign-on and discretionary bonuses. Sign-on bonuses are used only when necessary to attract highly skilled officers to the Company. Generally, they are used to incentivize candidates to leave their current employers or may be used to offset the loss of unvested compensation they may forfeit as a result of leaving their current employers.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">Long-Term Cash Incentive Compensation<b style="font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">.</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">2019 LTIP</i>. In December&#160;2019, our Board of Directors approved the Amended and Restated Apria Healthcare Group,&#160;Inc. Long-Term Incentive Plan (2019&#160;&#8211; 2021 With Successive Annual Extension Options) (which was assumed by the Company in connection with our IPO and renamed the Second Amended and Restated Apria,&#160;Inc. Long-Term Incentive Plan (2019-2021 With Successive Annual Extension Options), the &#8220;2019 LTIP&#8221;) and awarded long-term cash incentive awards to our named executive officers under the 2019 LTIP for the performance period beginning January&#160;1, 2019 and ending December&#160;31, 2021. The purpose of the 2019 LTIP is to incentivize free cash flow improvement and the transformational changes needed to position the Company properly for the future.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">In June&#160;2020, our Board of Directors awarded additional long-term cash incentive awards to our named executive officers under the 2019 LTIP for the performance period beginning January&#160;1, 2020 and ending December&#160;31, 2022. Mr.&#160;Starck was awarded an award with a target value of $200,000 and Ms.&#160;Morris was awarded an award with a target value of $100,000. Messrs.&#160;Smyth, Walker and Litkovitz were each awarded an award with a target value of $75,000.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The 2019 LTIP award opportunities are based on the achievement of specified cumulative free cash flow targets during the applicable performance periods. Based on achievement of the cumulative performance goals a participant can earn between 50% of their target award amount for threshold achievement and 200% of their target award amount for maximum achievement. See &#8220;Narrative Disclosure to Summary Compensation Table and Grants of Plan-Based Awards in 2020 Table&#8212;Terms of Long-Term Cash Incentive Awards&#8212;2019 LTIP Awards&#8221; below for a discussion of the vesting and other terms of these awards.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Following our IPO, pursuant to the terms of the 2019 LTIP, the 2019 LTIP awards will be settled in shares of our common stock issued pursuant to our Omnibus Incentive Plan (as described below), with the number of shares determined by dividing the actual amount of each executive&#8217;s award by $22.11, the volume-weighted average price of a share of our common stock over the 20 trading&#160;days following our IPO, beginning on the first trading date of our common stock on Nasdaq. The shares in respect of the 2019 LTIP awards will be delivered no later than March&#160;15th of the&#160;year following the final&#160;year of the applicable performance period, in all cases subject to the applicable participant remaining employed on the applicable payment date. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in the event that an executive is terminated without cause following our IPO, any remaining payments will be made in a lump sum as soon as administratively practicable following such termination.</p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">95</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">Long-Term Equity Incentive Compensation<b style="font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">.</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Holdings Units. </i>Prior to our IPO, the board of directors of Holdings, our parent entity prior to our IPO, determined to grant to our management employees, including our named executive officers, long-term incentive awards that were designed to promote our interests by providing our management employees with the opportunity to acquire equity interests as an incentive for the recipient to remain in our service. The Holdings board of directors granted these long-term incentive awards to our named executive officers in the form of Class&#160;B Units and Class&#160;C Units of Holdings (together, &#8220;Holdings Units&#8221;).</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Class&#160;B and Class&#160;C Units of Holdings are limited liability company profits interests having economic characteristics similar to SARs and representing the right to share in any increase in the equity value of Holdings that exceeds specified thresholds. For a Class&#160;B Unit, the threshold is the value of a Class&#160;A Unit of Holdings on the grant date which was generally $1.00. Therefore, a Class&#160;B Unit generally has a value at any given time equal to the value of a Class&#160;A Unit minus $1.00. For a Class&#160;C Unit, the threshold was $2.00. Therefore, a Class&#160;C Unit has a value at any given time equal to the value of a Class&#160;A Unit minus $2.00. Certain Class&#160;B Units have a higher threshold representing the estimated fair value of a Class&#160;A Unit on the applicable grant date.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Generally, the Class&#160;B Units of Holdings were divided into a time-vesting portion (2/3 of the Class&#160;B Units granted) and a performance-vesting portion (1/3 of the Class&#160;B Units granted). All Class&#160;C Units are performance-vesting. See &#8220;Narrative Disclosure to Summary Compensation Table and Grants of Plan-Based Awards in 2020 Table&#8212;Terms of Equity Awards&#8212;Holdings Units&#8221; below for a discussion of the vesting and other terms of these equity units.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">As a condition to receiving their Holdings Units, each named executive officer was required to enter into a subscription agreement with us and to become a party to the Holdings limited liability company agreement, as well as a securityholders agreement. These agreements generally governed the named executive officer&#8217;s rights with respect to the Holdings Units.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Class&#160;B Units.</i> The Class&#160;B Units of Holdings granted to Ms.&#160;Morris and Messrs.&#160;Smyth, Walker and Litkovitz between 2009 and 2013 were divided into a time-vesting portion (2/3 of the Class&#160;B Units granted) and a performance-vesting portion (1/3 of the Class&#160;B Units granted). The Class&#160;B Units of Holdings granted to Mr.&#160;Starck in 2012 were 50% time-vesting and 50% performance-vesting. Mr.&#160;Starck&#8217;s Class&#160;B Units also contained a catchup provision that provided for the opportunity to participate in the increase in the equity value of Holdings prior to the date his Class&#160;B Units were granted.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Class&#160;C Units.</i> All Class&#160;C Units of Holdings granted to Ms.&#160;Morris and Messrs.&#160;Smyth, Walker and Litkovitz were performance-vesting and had the same vesting terms as the performance-vesting Class&#160;B Units. The performance-vesting Class&#160;B and Class&#160;C Units vested only if Blackstone received cash proceeds (not subject to any clawback, indemnity or similar contractual obligation) in respect of 25% (100% for Mr.&#160;Starck&#8217;s performance-vesting Class&#160;B Units) of its units equal to 200% of its aggregate capital contributions for such units.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">All time-vesting Class&#160;B Units are fully vested and, on June&#160;21, 2019, our Board of Directors determined it was appropriate to accelerate the vesting of all outstanding performance-vesting Class&#160;B Units. In addition, as a result of the 2020 Dividend described above, all outstanding Class&#160;C Units fully vested in accordance with their terms.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Call Option.</i> If (1)&#160;the named executive officer&#8217;s employment is terminated by us for &#8220;cause&#8221; (as defined in the applicable subscription agreement) or the named executive officer voluntarily resigns where grounds for cause exist or (2)&#160;the named executive officers breaches any of the restrictive covenants set forth below, then we have the right to purchase all of the named executive officer&#8217;s vested Class&#160;B or Class&#160;C Units at the lesser of fair market value thereof and cost, which means that such vested Class&#160;B or Class&#160;C Units will be effectively forfeited.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Restrictive Covenants.</i> As a condition of receiving the Class&#160;B and Class&#160;C Units, our named executive officers agreed to certain restrictive covenants, including confidentiality of information, noncompetition, non-solicitation and non-disparagement covenants. The confidentiality and non-disparagement covenants have an indefinite term, whereas the non-competition covenant has a term of one&#160;year and the non-solicitation covenant has a term of two&#160;years.</p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">96</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Clawback.</i> The Company has the right to &#8220;clawback&#8221; and recover any gains the named executive officer may have realized with respect to his or her Class&#160;B Units or Class&#160;C Units if he or she violates any of the restrictive covenants described above or we discover after a termination of employment that grounds existed for &#8220;cause&#8221;.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Conversion of Holdings Units.</i> In connection with our IPO, all vested Holdings Units were surrendered in exchange for vested shares of our common stock. The number of vested shares of common stock delivered was determined in a manner intended to replicate the respective economic value associated with the Class&#160;B and Class&#160;C Units of Holdings, as applicable, based upon the valuation derived from the IPO price.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">The following table sets forth the number and value of vested shares of our common stock that each of our named executive officers received in exchange for their vested Class&#160;B Units and vested Class&#160;C Units.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><font style="margin-bottom:12pt;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</font></p><div approved the Apria Healthcare Group&#160;Inc. 2015 Stock Plan (which was assumed by Apria,&#160;Inc. in connection with our IPO and renamed the &#8220;Apria,&#160;Inc. 2015 Stock Plan,&#8221; the &#8220;2015 Stock Plan&#8221;) pursuant to which SARs were granted to employees of Apria Healthcare Group and its affiliates, including our named executive officers. All SARs granted under the 2015 Plan are time-vesting. See &#8220;Narrative Disclosure to Summary Compensation Table and Grants of Plan-Based Awards in 2020 Table&#8212;Terms of Equity Awards&#8212;Stock Appreciation Rights of Apria Healthcare Group&#8221; below for a discussion of the vesting and other terms of the SARs.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">In 2020, in order to motivate continued performance and enhance retention, we granted additional SARs to each of the named executive officers in the following amounts: Mr.&#160;Starck, 122,449 SARs; Ms.&#160;Morris, 61,189 SARs; and Messrs.&#160;Smyth, Walker and Litkovitz were each granted 22,999 SARs, respectively.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">2020 Dividend. </i>As described above, on December&#160;4, 2020, our Board of Directors declared, and on December&#160;11, 2020, paid the 2020 Dividend, a $201.79 per share dividend to common stockholders. Under the terms of the 2015 Plan, an adjustment to the outstanding SARs was determined to be equitable and necessary in order to prevent the dilution or enlargement of benefits under the 2015 Plan. Holders of vested SARs were entitled to an immediate cash payment per SAR equal to the lower of (i)&#160;the per share dividend amount and (ii)&#160;an amount equal to the difference between $495.13 and the strike price of such vested SAR. Accordingly, in addition to certain strike price reductions, the named executive officers received the following cash payments with respect to their vested SARs: Mr.&#160;Starck, $2,198,152; Ms.&#160;Morris, $1,021,363; Mr.&#160;Smyth, $469,731; Mr.&#160;Walker, $708,174; and Mr.&#160;Litkovitz, $381,930. For holders of vested SARs who received the cash payment in clause (ii)&#160;above, the strike price of each such vested SAR was reduced by an amount equal to the per share dividend amount less the cash payment per vested SAR. With respect to outstanding unvested SARs, we reduced the per share exercise prices of such SARs by the per share dividend amount; provided, that with respect to unvested SARs for which such strike price reduction would have resulted in the strike price for such unvested SAR being less than $73.34, the strike price for such unvested SAR was reduced to $73.34 and the holder of each such unvested SAR is entitled to receive a cash payment equal to the difference between the per share dividend amount and the strike price reduction when such unvested SAR vests. Accordingly, in addition to certain strike price reductions, the named executive officers will be entitled to receive the following cash payments with respect to their unvested SARs: Mr.&#160;Starck, $116,325; Ms.&#160;Morris, $116,325; Mr.&#160;Smyth $29,068; Mr.&#160;Walker, $116,325; and Mr.&#160;Litkovitz, $29,068. In accordance with FASB ASC Topic 718 changes to the SARs associated with the 2020 Dividend were accounted for as modifications. As such, the fair value of each award immediately before and after the modifications were compared and no incremental stock compensation was recognized.</p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">97</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Chief Financial Officer RSU Award. </i>In 2018, our Board of Directors determined it was appropriate to enter into a letter agreement with Ms.&#160;Morris that provides for an additional long-term equity incentive award in the form of restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) upon the occurrence of an initial public offering or in connection with a change of control. Ms. Morris elected to have the Tranche I RSUs settled in cash and the Company delivered such cash payment promptly following the closing of the IPO. In the event that Ms.&#160;Morris elects for the remaining RSUs to be settled in cash, the Company will deliver the cash in respect of the remaining RSUs upon the applicable vesting dates. In the event Ms.&#160;Morris elects for the remaining RSUs to be settled in shares of common stock, shares of common stock underlying vested RSUs will be delivered as soon as reasonably practicable, but in no event will any shares be delivered prior to the date of the first open trading window of the Company that is at least six&#160;months following the closing of the IPO.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Broad-based Employee Benefits</font><b style="font-weight:bold;">. </b>We provide to all of our employees, including our named executive officers, broad-based benefits that are intended to attract and retain employees while providing them with retirement and health and welfare security. Broad-based employee benefits include:</p><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"></td><td style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;">&#9679;</td><td style="padding:0pt;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">a 401(k)&#160;savings plan;</font></td></tr></table><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"></td><td style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;">&#9679;</td><td style="padding:0pt;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">paid vacation, sick time and holidays;</font></td></tr></table><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"></td><td style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;">&#9679;</td><td style="padding:0pt;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">medical, dental, vision, life and accident insurance, disability coverage, dependent care and healthcare flexible spending accounts; and</font></td></tr></table><table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;table-layout:fixed;width:100%;border:0pt;"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"></td><td style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;">&#9679;</td><td style="padding:0pt;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">employee assistance program benefits.</font></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:12pt;"></div><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Under our 401(k)&#160;savings plan, we match a portion of the funds set aside by the employee. The maximum match available under the 401(k)&#160;savings plan is 25% of the first 8% of the employee&#8217;s eligible contributions per pay period. For participants who became an employee before January&#160;1, 2007, all matching contributions by us vest 20% after one&#160;year of service, 40% after two&#160;years of service and are fully vested after three&#160;years of service. For participants who became an employee on or after January&#160;1, 2007, all matching contributions by us become fully vested after three&#160;years of service. In addition, we may make non-elective contributions under the 401(k)&#160;savings plan, subject to statutory limitations imposed by Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;).</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">At no cost to the employee, we also provide $50,000 in basic life and accident insurance coverage insurance. The employee may also select supplemental life and accident insurance, for a premium to be paid by the employee.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Supplemental Executive Benefits</font><b style="font-weight:bold;">. </b>We provide a nonqualified deferred compensation plan, which is also intended to attract and retain executives. The nonqualified deferred compensation plan is intended to promote retention by providing </p></div><div style="clear:both;margin-bottom:30pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">98</p></div></div><hr style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;color:#000000;height:2pt;line-height:0;margin-bottom:30pt;margin-left:10.35%;margin-right:10.35%;margin-top:30pt;page-break-after:always;width:79.3%;border-width:0;"><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:10.35%;padding-right:10.35%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:21.6pt;min-height:41.75pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</font></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">to participants a long-term savings opportunity on a tax-efficient basis. Under the nonqualified deferred compensation plan, participants may defer certain portions of their salary, annual bonus and annual 401(k)&#160;savings plan refund offset amount, as more fully explained in the narrative following the Nonqualified Deferred Compensation for 2020 Table below. In 2020, the Company matched 100% of participant contributions to the nonqualified deferred compensation plan up to 4% of the participant&#8217;s salary. For plan&#160;year 2021, the Company will again match 100% of a participant&#8217;s salary contributions to the nonqualified deferred compensation plan up to 4% of the participant&#8217;s salary. Participants are 100% vested in matching contributions if they remain employed at the end of the applicable&#160;year.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Severance Arrangements and Non-Competition Agreements</font><b style="font-weight:bold;">. </b>Our Board of Directors believes that severance arrangements are necessary to attract and retain the talent necessary for our long-term success. Our Board of Directors views our severance arrangements as recruitment and retention devices that help secure the continued employment and dedication of our named executive officers, including when we are considering strategic alternatives.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Each of our named executive officers has a severance arrangement with us, either as part of their employment agreement or as a separate severance agreement. Under the terms of these severance arrangements, each of the named executive officers is entitled to severance benefits if he or she is terminated by us without cause or by him or her as a result of constructive termination or for good reason, as applicable. See &#8220;&#8212;Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change-in-Control&#8212;Severance Arrangements&#8221; below for descriptions of these arrangements.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">In December&#160;2020, in recognition of his service and contributions to the Company we entered into a letter agreement with Mr.&#160;Smyth governing the terms of his retirement, which agreement is described under &#8220;Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change-in-Control&#8212;Raoul Smyth Retirement Agreement&#8221; below.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 18pt;">Actions Take in Connection with our IPO</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Post-IPO Long-Term Incentive Plan</font><b style="font-weight:bold;">.</b> In connection with our IPO, our Board of Directors adopted, and our stockholders approved, our Omnibus Incentive Plan, which will allow us to implement a new market-based long-term incentive program to align our executive compensation package with similarly situated public companies. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Compensation Committee Report</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The compensation committee has reviewed and discussed the Compensation Discussion and Analysis with management. Based on its review and discussion with management, the compensation committee recommended to the Board of Directors that the Compensation Discussion and Analysis be included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Submitted by the compensation committee of our Board of Directors:</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;">Neil P.
